title: vcpkg_fixup_cmake_targets does not correctly handle generator expressions

labels.name: category:vcpkg-bug
labels.description: The issue is with the vcpkg system (including helper scripts in `scripts/cmake/`)

body:
### Short summary

The [`vcpkg_fixup_cmake_targets()` function](https://github.com/Microsoft/vcpkg/blob/master/scripts/cmake/vcpkg_fixup_cmake_targets.cmake) does not handle generator expressions. You do not need to use generators explicitly for this to come up, because they are used internally by `target_link_libraries` if you specify the `debug` or `optimized` qualifier. This results in a very confusing error when you come to link against a library affected by this.


### More detail

I am using the following chain of dependencies:

 * An internal application, which I am building with CMake. This depends on ...
 * ... an internal library, let's call it XYZ, which I have written a vcpkg port for. This depends on ...
 * ... the Windows pthreads library. This already has a vcpkg port.

However, pthreads does not have a CMake config, so I have to find it manually in the `CMakeLists.txt` for XYZ:

    find_library(PTHREADS_LIB pthreadsVC2)
    find_library(PTHREADS_LIBD pthreadsVC2d PATH_SUFFIXES debug/lib)
    find_path(PTHREADS_INCLUDE "pthread.h")
    target_link_libraries(xyz PUBLIC debug ${PTHREADS_LIBD} optimized ${PTHREADS_LIB})
    target_include_directories(xyz PUBLIC ${PTHREADS_INCLUDE})

On the other hand, I *do* export targets for XYZ and include that from a CMake config file, so the application can just use `find_package()`:

    find_package(xyz)
    target_link_libraries(my_application PUBLIC xyz)

However, attempting to build and link causes the following bewildering error:

    LINK : fatal error LNK1104: cannot open file '$<1:$<0:opencv_calib3d.obj' [C:\src\my_application\build\my_application.vcxproj]

The mention of OpenCV is a red herring. The my_application target did depend on it, but after I removed all references to it and rebuilt everything I still got a confusing message involving dollar symbols and less than symbols:

    LINK : fatal error LNK1104: cannot open file '$<1:.obj' [C:\src\my_application\build\my_application.vcxproj]

It turns out the problem is to do with my library's `xyz-targets.cmake` file containing absolute paths to the installation directory:

    set_target_properties(xyz PROPERTIES
      INTERFACE_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES "C:/src/vcpkg/installed/x64-windows-static/include;${_IMPORT_PREFIX}/include"
      INTERFACE_LINK_LIBRARIES "\$<\$<CONFIG:DEBUG>:C:/src/vcpkg/installed/x64-windows-static/debug/lib/pthreadsVC2d.lib>;\$<\$<NOT:\$<CONFIG:DEBUG>>:C:/src/vcpkg/installed/x64-windows-static/lib/pthreadsVC2.lib>"
    )

This is detected [in by these regexs in `vcpkg_fixup_cmake_targets()`](https://github.com/Microsoft/vcpkg/blob/e441811bc283fdbff8c5a5de98eee45c1b1faa5e/scripts/cmake/vcpkg_fixup_cmake_targets.cmake#L131-L140). However, they do not correctly handle the generator expressions, resulting in this in the fixed-up xyz-targets.cmake, with the leftover `_INVALID_ROOT_` string and mismatched angle brackets:

    set_target_properties(xyz PROPERTIES
      INTERFACE_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES "${_IMPORT_PREFIX}/include"
      INTERFACE_LINK_LIBRARIES "\$<\$<CONFIG:DEBUG>:\$<\$<NOT:\$<CONFIG:DEBUG>>:_INVALID_ROOT_/lib/pthreadsVC2.lib>"
    )


### Workaround

The workaround for this problem (or arguably even the correct thing to do in the first place) is to avoid the library dependency ending up in your targets file. If your library is dynamically linked then you can do this by passing the `PRIVATE` specifier to `target_link_libraries()`. For static libraries this specifier is ignored, but you can just omit the `target_link_libraries()` call altogether. Another possibility, that works both ways, is to use the $<BUILD_INTERFACE:...> generator, which works so long as it is the outermost generator in `target_link_libraries()`:

    target_link_libraries(xyz PUBLIC 
        $<BUILD_INTERFACE:$<IF:$<CONFIG:Debug>, ${PTHREADS_LIBD}, ${PTHREADS_LIB}>>
    )

Whichever these you use, you will also have to compensate by manually adding the dependency on the target in the corresponding `xyz-config.cmake` file after including `xyz-targets.cmake`.

### Other points

 * I notice that these regexs are only applied to libname-targets.cmake and LibnameTargets.cmake, but in principle the targets file could be called anything. In fact, until recently I had set the `EXPORT` name directly to `libname-config.cmake`, believing that it was what you are meant to do. I don't think I'm the only person to make this mistake.
 * Unrelated: In the `find_library()` call for the debug build of the pthreads library, I am not sure why I need the `PATH_SUFFIXES debug/lib` parameter. Shouldn't that path already be searched? It didn't seem to work without it though.
